title: Italian Game — Basic Setup
description: Meet the Italian Game: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4. See it on the board, understand the ideas, then play the key move yourself.

steps.text: Welcome! The **Italian Game** is one of the oldest and most instructive openings: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4. White occupies the center, develops pieces quickly, and points the bishop at Black's weakest square, f7. Watch the moves first, then you'll try them yourself.
Play the demonstration to see the Italian Game take shape move by move.
comments: 1.e4 — grabs the center and opens lines for the bishop and queen.
1...e5 — Black mirrors, fighting for the center.
2.Nf3 — develops the knight and attacks the e5 pawn.
2...Nc6 — defends e5 and develops toward the center.
3.Bc4 — the Italian bishop! It eyes the f7 pawn, Black's most vulnerable point.

steps.prompt: You're playing White after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6. Find the Italian bishop move.
hints: Look at your light-squared bishop — it hasn't moved yet.
Which developing square also stares at Black's f7 pawn?
The Italian is 3.Bc4 — develop the bishop there.
steps.continue_text: That's it — 3.Bc4 is the Italian Game. The bishop develops with a purpose: pressure on f7 and quick castling behind it.

steps.prompt: Now you're Black after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4. Continue your development — which natural move do you play?
hints: Black needs to develop a piece and prepare the king's safety.
Two classical answers: bring out the king's knight or the king's bishop.
3...Nf6 (Two Knights) or 3...Bc5 (Giuoco Piano) are both main-line moves.
steps.continue_text: Correct — 3...Nf6 or 3...Bc5 are the two main replies, and both follow the same principles: develop, control the center, prepare to castle.

steps.text: You've learned the Italian Game setup: **control the center with e4, develop with Nf3, and place the bishop on c4 aiming at f7** — then castle quickly. Tomorrow we'll dig into *why* each move matters, move by move. Lesson complete!

completion.text: Lesson complete! You played the Italian bishop move and answered Black's main development. Next up: why e4, Nf3, and Bc4 are played.
